statement:
(i) Suppose that
$$S=\int\frac{\cos x}{\cos x+\sin x}\,dx\quad\text{and}\quad T=\int\frac{\sin x}{\cos x+\sin x}\,dx.$$
By considering $S+T$ and $S-T$, determine $S$ and $T$.

(ii) Evaluate
$$\int_{1/4}^{1/2}(1-4x)\sqrt{\frac{1}{x}-1}\,dx$$
by using the substitution $x=\sin^2 t$.
solution:
(i) Adding,
$$S+T=\int\frac{\cos x+\sin x}{\cos x+\sin x}\,dx=\int 1\,dx=x+C_1.$$

Subtracting,
$$S-T=\int\frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\cos x+\sin x}\,dx.$$
The numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so
$$S-T=\ln|\cos x+\sin x|+C_2.$$

Solving the two equations:
$$S=\frac{(S+T)+(S-T)}{2}=\frac{x+\ln(\cos x+\sin x)}{2}+C,$$
$$T=\frac{(S+T)-(S-T)}{2}=\frac{x-\ln(\cos x+\sin x)}{2}+C'.$$

(ii) Let $x=\sin^2 t$, so $dx=2\sin t\cos t\,dt$. When $x=1/4$, $\sin t=1/2$ so $t=\pi/6$; when $x=1/2$, $\sin t=1/\sqrt2$ so $t=\pi/4$.

Also $1-4x=1-4\sin^2 t$ and $\sqrt{\frac1x-1}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\sin^2 t}{\sin^2 t}}=\frac{\cos t}{\sin t}$.

Therefore the integral becomes
$$\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}(1-4\sin^2 t)\cdot\frac{\cos t}{\sin t}\cdot 2\sin t\cos t\,dt=2\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}(1-4\sin^2 t)\cos^2 t\,dt.$$

Now $1-4\sin^2t=(1-2\sin^2t)-2\sin^2t=\cos2t-2\sin^2t$. A cleaner approach is to expand $(1-4\sin^2t)\cos^2t$:
$$(1-4\sin^2t)\cos^2t=\cos^2t-4\sin^2t\cos^2t=\cos^2t-\sin^22t.$$

Using $\cos^2t=\tfrac{1+\cos2t}{2}$ and $\sin^22t=\tfrac{1-\cos4t}{2}$:
$$2\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}\left(\frac{1+\cos2t}{2}-\frac{1-\cos4t}{2}\right)dt=\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}(\cos2t+\cos4t)\,dt.$$

This equals
$$\left[\frac{\sin2t}{2}+\frac{\sin4t}{4}\right]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}=\left(\frac{\sin\tfrac{\pi}{2}}{2}+\frac{\sin\pi}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3}}{2}+\frac{\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}}{4}\right).$$

$$=\left(\frac12+0\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt3/2}{2}+\frac{\sqrt3/2}{4}\right)=\frac12-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}-\frac{\sqrt3}{8}=\frac12-\frac{3\sqrt3}{8}.$$

So the integral equals $\boxed{\tfrac{1}{2}-\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{8}}$.
hints: For S+T and S-T, note that cos(x)-sin(x) is the derivative of cos(x)+sin(x).
Use the substitution x=sin^2(t) and simplify the square root.
Use double-angle identities to integrate the resulting trig expression.
